subject: Cloud listing fee renewal — coordination and negotiation plan
messages:
From: Megan Park <megan@cloudmarketplaceconsulting.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Listing program renewal — proposed rate adjustments and timeline

Hi Rishi / Vanessa,

Hope you’re both well. Our records show Redwood’s annual listing agreement across AWS and GCP is up for renewal on 2027-07-15. The platform teams have proposed a modest rate adjustment to the listing fee structure to reflect new marketplace packaging. High level: a +10% uplift on the base fee, or an option for a 6-month bridge credit program if Redwood signs a 12-month commitment by July 1.

Can we set a 30-minute slot this week to walk through the updated rate card and potential credit structures? I can share the new rate card and a short allocation sheet ahead of time.

Attachments: proposal_summary.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Park
Senior Marketplace Consultant
Cloud Marketplace Consulting
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Megan Park <megan@cloudmarketplaceconsulting.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Listing program renewal — proposed rate adjustments and timeline

Thanks Megan — available Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT. Vanessa / Karthik, are you able to join?

A few items for the meeting:
- Current usage/transaction volumes by marketplace (AWS / GCP) for the trailing 12 months.
- Any marketplace credits or co-sell incentives Redwood received in the last 12 months.
- If the uplift is mandatory vs. negotiable for higher committed spend.

Megan — please send the rate card and the bridge-credit example before the call. If there’s a standard DocuSign for the commit, include that link as well.

– Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Listing program renewal — negotiation approach (internal)

Forwarding the vendor note — quick internal thinking before the call:

Topline negotiation levers (suggested):
- Push for a conditional uplift: allow +10% only if partner marketing/co-sell revenue targets are hit; otherwise baseline stays flat.
- Request a 6-month bridge credit (as Megan suggested) to smooth the FY impact; tie to PR/launch milestones.
- Ask for a first-year onboarding credit for private deployments (we still have 3 active pilots).
- Seek a written cap on future automatic uplifts (contractual language).

Action for Laura: can you sign off on escalating to Marketplace Ops for a one-time credit approval up to $75k? We can present the use case: Dedicated launches + top-of-funnel marketing drive.

Vanessa
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Gomez <aws-partner@amazon.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Listing program renewal — proposed rate adjustments and timeline

Hi team — appreciate the note and the constructive approach. For transparency: the 10% adjustment reflects updated packaging for premium placement tiers across a subset of regions. That said, we do have two options that may help Redwood preserve unit economics:

1) Co-sell credit: up to 50% credit on listing fees for qualified co-sell opportunities (requires joint pipeline registration).
2) Transition credit: a 6-month phased credit that applies when a 12-month commitment is executed before July 1.

Attached is the current AWS rate card (aws_listing_rate_card_v4.pdf) and a short checklist for qualifying co-sell credits.

If you can share expected ARR from marketplace-sourced sales and the pilot timelines, I can tee up the credit approval conversation internally. Happy to join Thursday’s call.

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
Program Manager — AWS Marketplace Partnerships
Attachments: aws_listing_rate_card_v4.pdf, aws_co-sell_qualification.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <aws-partner@amazon.com>, Megan Park <megan@cloudmarketplaceconsulting.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Listing program renewal — coordination and negotiation plan

Thanks Alicia / Megan — useful context and the rate card looks clear. Quick internal summary and next steps from our side: 

Summary:
- Marketplace partner has proposed a baseline +10% on premium placement tiers, but two mitigation paths are available: a co-sell credit and a 6-month transition credit tied to an early 12-month commit.
- We have three leverage points: (1) committed ARR, (2) co-marketing / co-sell motion, (3) showcasing Dedicated pilot pipeline to justify transition credit.

Action items (owners):
- Rishi: compile trailing-12-month marketplace-attributed ARR and expected pipeline by 06-11-2027. (upload to HubSpot deal DL-8742).
- Karthik: finance to model the net impact of +10% uplift vs. taking the 6-month bridge credit — due 06-09-2027.
- Vanessa: prepare a short ask deck (1–2 slides) for Marketplace Ops to request a one-time $75k credit — due 06-08-2027. Attach to the deal.
- Laura: approve escalation for credit negotiation (please confirm by 06-08-2027).

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_renewal_playbook.docx, redwood_messaging_deck.pptx (stubs)

We’ll reconvene after the finance model and the deck — if Marketplace Ops confirms co-sell credit eligibility we should be able to neutralize the uplift.

Thanks all,
– Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
